title: Insights and lessons learned from integrating environmental considerations into U.S. stock assessments
content:
Abstract
Stock assessments are an essential tool used to support sustainable fisheries management through evaluating the state of a population and assessing the sustainability of different harvest levels. Interest in developing environment-informed stock assessments has been increasing in the U.S. and globally. However, despite the increasing evidence that not accounting for impacts of environmental change on population processes can introduce substantial uncertainty into models, and ultimately, fisheries management, to date very few stock assessments have successfully integrated environmental information into their population models. Here, we review case studies where scientists have had varying degrees of success in integrating environmental and climate data into the stock assessment and fisheries management process to inform catch advice in the U.S. For each case study, we describe the underlying process research supporting the environment-stock linkage(s) explored, the method for incorporating and evaluating the environment-population relationship(s) in the stock assessment, and the effect the integration of the environment-population relationship(s) had on both the assessment and subsequent management advice. We then look across case studies to identify common challenges, lessons learned, and the factors contributing to both the successful incorporation of environmental information into operational management and the instances where such information was not adopted or was subsequently removed from models. Several key lessons emerged from these case studies, including the importance of: field observations to monitor and identify changes; consistent long-term time-series data to develop environmental indicators; clear evidence for mechanistic relationships; continually testing and validating relationships; support for research and development and; co-development and resource user engagement. These case studies show that successful integration of environmental data is feasible, and the lessons learned provide useful insights into how to move towards more holistic environment-informed assessments to promote effective fisheries management.
